project.name: grouped-nf4-gemm
project.summary: Triton kernels for 4-bit MoE inference: grouped NF4/MXFP4 GEMM, INT4 GEMV, FP8 paged attention, and CPU/NVMe expert streaming.
project.role: Owns the packed-expert kernels (grouped NF4 and native MXFP4 GEMMs), the decode kernels (int4-b32 GEMV, FP8 paged attention, decode glue), the packing and reference operations, and the host/NVMe arena primitives; experts4bit-qlora drives them and decides which bytes live where.

related_projects.name: experts4bit-qlora
related_projects.relationship: consumer side: experts4bit-qlora[fast] installs this package; it owns model loading, quantization orchestration, adapters, training, residency integration and serving

non_goals: a serving engine or a vLLM replacement: this is a kernel package driven by experts4bit-qlora
operating systems other than Linux for the kernels (triton is Linux-only); ROCm/XPU are port targets, not supported
models that already fit in bf16 with headroom: the grouped kernel loses at small shapes and to a CUDA-graphed per-expert loop at some decode shapes (claims gnf4.kernel.graphed-baseline-decode-loses)
silent fallbacks: a kernel call on CPU raises and names the pure-torch reference

capabilities.problem: Dequantising every active expert to bf16 before its matmul is the bottleneck of 4-bit MoE inference; compute the grouped expert GEMM directly on the NF4-packed weights instead.
symptoms: grouped GEMM over bitsandbytes NF4 packed weights
capabilities.solution: gemm_4bit_grouped runs one Triton launch for all active experts over the bitsandbytes gemm_4bit NF4 layout (LUT decode to fp32 in registers, blockwise absmax scaling, fp32 accumulation, bf16 epilogue); dequant_ref is the pure-torch oracle it is asserted against; dgrad_4bit_grouped is the one-launch training backward.
model_families: any fused-expert MoE whose experts are packed in the bitsandbytes NF4 gemm_4bit layout (Qwen3-MoE, OLMoE, Mixtral, GraniteMoe, Gemma-4 text tower via experts4bit-qlora)

environment.python: >=3.11 tested in CI (pyproject says >=3.9; 3.9/3.10 are not tested)
accelerator: NVIDIA CUDA GPU, sm_80 or newer (sm_120 is the primary serving target)

limitations: Loses to a CUDA-graphed per-expert baseline at some decode shapes (claim gnf4.kernel.graphed-baseline-decode-loses); shapes below the routing threshold go back to the reference path (docs/STATUS.md)
CUDA + Triton only; calling the kernel on CPU raises and names dequant_ref
The fidelity claim is measured against fp32 accumulation on NVIDIA tensor cores; other backends must re-measure (docs/PORTABILITY.md)

capabilities.problem: Serve or train a MoE whose experts are released as MXFP4 (gpt-oss, DeepSeek-V4, Kimi lineage) directly from the checkpoint's own bytes, without re-quantising them.
symptoms: MXFP4 to bf16 dequant costs VRAM and time
serve MXFP4 experts from the released bytes
capabilities.solution: gemm_mxfp4_grouped is the table-swap of the NF4 kernel over native blocks [E, N, K//2] + e8m0 scales [E, N, K//32]; gemv_mxfp4_b32 is its decode-grade GEMV; mxfp4_loader.to_kernel_shapes views the released tensors in kernel layout with no copy; mxfp4_qlora and mxfp4_native_load train LoRA over the frozen native stacks.

environment.python: >=3.11 tested in CI (pyproject says >=3.9; 3.9/3.10 are not tested)
accelerator: NVIDIA CUDA GPU, sm_80 or newer (sm_120 is the primary serving target)

limitations: A uniform int4 grid cannot represent e2m1 levels: do not quantise-bake an already-MXFP4 checkpoint to NF4 or int4 (README)
gemv_mxfp4_b32 re-streams weights per row: it is a decode lever for a handful of rows; batched rows use the grouped GEMM or the consumer's NF4 path

capabilities.problem: Single-token (decode) expert and attention projections on 4-bit weights are bandwidth-bound; an int4 GEMV with 32-wide scales and a calibrated packer serves them near the memory ceiling.
symptoms: split-K GEMV for MoE experts at batch 1
capabilities.solution: quant_x_rows quantises activation rows to int8 with per-32 scales; gemv_int4_b32 runs the split-K int4-b32 GEMV over packed [E, N, K//2] + fp16 scales [E, N, K//32] (reduce_partials folds the split-K sum and bf16 cast into one launch); pack_int4_b32 is the round-to-nearest packer and gptq_pack_int4_b32 + HessianAccumulator the calibrated one; gemm_int4_b32_grouped_captured is the capture-legal batched variant.
model_families: any expert or projection weight packed with pack_int4_b32 / gptq_pack_int4_b32 (driven by experts4bit-qlora's serve lanes)

environment.python: >=3.11 tested in CI (pyproject says >=3.9; 3.9/3.10 are not tested)
accelerator: NVIDIA CUDA GPU, sm_80 or newer (sm_120 is the primary serving target)

limitations: The int4-b32 GEMV and the calibrated packer are measured-private (claims gnf4.serve.int4-b32-gemv, gnf4.serve.gptq-pack-int4-b32): the receipts live in the consumer's private audit tree
Split-K on the decode GEMV was refuted once and ships dormant (claim gnf4.retired.splitk-gemv records the refutation); the shipped plan is the measured one
Whether int4 experts pass a quality gate is the consumer's per-family question (experts4bit-qlora docs/STATUS.md): small-active-parameter models fail it with round-to-nearest packing

capabilities.problem: A 4-bit MoE serving path needs a paged decode attention over an fp8 KV cache and the small fused kernels around the expert GEMM (norms, rotary, router epilogue, activation, combine).
symptoms: FP8 paged attention for MoE serving
sliding window and attention sinks in paged decode
fused RMSNorm rotary router epilogue at batch 1
capabilities.solution: fp8_kv quantises and appends KV blocks in e4m3 with per-(token, head) or grouped scales; fp8_paged_decode_attention is the paged decode kernel with sliding windows, sinks, custom scale and per-layer KV geometry, asserted against paged_attn_ref; int4_b32 carries the decode glue (rmsnorm_rows, rmsnorm_resid_rows, scaled_resid_add_rows, rope_norm_heads, rope_heads, router_epilogue, swiglu_rows, combine_rows).
model_families: driven by experts4bit-qlora's paged engine for Qwen3-MoE, OLMoE, GraniteMoe, gpt-oss, Gemma-4, Mixtral

environment.python: >=3.11 tested in CI (pyproject says >=3.9; 3.9/3.10 are not tested)
accelerator: NVIDIA CUDA GPU, sm_80 or newer (sm_120 is the primary serving target)

limitations: The f32 compute modes of the paged kernel fail on triton 3.4 (claim gnf4.open.f32-compute-modes-triton34 records the open item); the fp8 compute modes are the serving default
The decode glue kernels are measured-private (claim gnf4.serve.decode-glue-kernels)
KV budgets in docs/context-budgets.md are rung-one (A2000) numbers; pending rows must not be promoted

capabilities.problem: The expert weights do not fit in VRAM, or not even in host RAM: stream them from pinned host memory or from an on-disk expert arena on NVMe.
symptoms: stream MoE experts from host RAM
bake an NF4 arena to disk
serve a 235B MoE from host RAM
capabilities.solution: nvme_arena.bake / bake_expert_tensors relocate a checkpoint's expert tensors into a page-aligned arena with an index and manifest; nvme_bake_nf4.bake_nf4 quantises at bake; nvme_reader.ArenaReader reads it with O_DIRECT queues; nvme_residency.ColdTier and row_pool.RowPool hold the hot rows in pinned DRAM; arena_experts.ArenaExpertSource fetches per-layer fused stacks; mxfp4_residency serves native MXFP4 arenas.
model_families: gpt-oss / DeepSeek-V4 / Kimi lineage MXFP4 arenas
any checkpoint whose experts the bake can enumerate

environment.python: >=3.11 tested in CI (pyproject says >=3.9; 3.9/3.10 are not tested)
accelerator: NVIDIA CUDA GPU for the serving tiers; the bake and verify are pure torch
special_requirements: pinned host RAM sized from measured free memory (capacity_for_bytes)
a local NVMe or fast block device for the arena; O_DIRECT reads

limitations: NVMe is a batch tier: per-token latency is bounded by the device link (claim gnf4.nvme.tier-batch-only)
Expert prefetch closed negative over four arcs (claim gnf4.flagship.prefetch-closed-negative)
The cold-engine 'free floor' premise was refuted (claim gnf4.cold-engine.phase0-premise-refuted); read docs/INDEX.md before quoting any cold-engine number

capabilities.problem: Prove that the quantised bytes a kernel serves are the checkpoint's released bytes, unchanged, before quoting any result.
symptoms: verify released checkpoint bytes were unchanged
does my arena match the checkpoint
capabilities.solution: mxfp4_loader.file_tensor_sha256 hashes a safetensors tensor's data-section bytes without loading or dequantising; provenance_table builds the per-tensor hash table for a snapshot; verify_arena_matches raises on any mismatch (a provenance failure is not a tolerance); nvme_arena.verify checks an arena against its source; python -m verify_provenance is the CLI.
model_families: any safetensors checkpoint; MXFP4 expert tensors for gpt-oss / DeepSeek-V4 / Kimi lineage

environment.python: >=3.11 tested in CI (pyproject says >=3.9; 3.9/3.10 are not tested)
accelerator: none: pure torch (a CUDA GPU is optional)
special_requirements: macOS/Windows: not validated by CI (the README's older note reports an import failure for the CPU quickstart there; _triton_shim is the mitigation)

limitations: A quantize-at-bake arena (nvme_bake_nf4) is a documented two-hop transform: its manifest's bake_mode says it is bit-identical to the quantiser's output, not to a bf16 release
Making the verifier pass on non-matching bytes is the highest-severity class in SECURITY.md; report privately
